nodes.label: The astronomy behind Planet Location Marker (ASTRONOMY.md)
Greenwich apparent sidereal time (GAST)
Julian calendar dates before 15 Oct 1582 (toCalendar, JDN)
nodes.rationale: Records of the time give Julian dates; one worldwide cut-over is a simplification (Britain switched in 1752, Russia in 1918).

nodes.label: Reduced accuracy badge (outside 1800-2200)
nodes.rationale: Uncertainty in Delta T dominates far from the present: about a minute of time around 1000, tens of minutes toward 3000.

nodes.label: EQJ frame (J2000 mean equator and equinox)
EQD frame (true equator and equinox of date)
Earth-fixed frame (EF)
Scene frame (+Y = J2000 pole, 1 unit = Earth radius)
S mapping EQJ -> scene ((x,y,z) -> (x,z,-y))
Matrix layout gotcha (Astronomy Engine rotation transpose, aeRotToM3)
nodes.rationale: RotateVector reads rot[j][i], so a row-major matrix needs the transpose; a test checks it against RotateVector to 1e-15.

nodes.label: earthMatrix = S*(PN*Rz(GAST))*S^T
Static sky, moving Earth (equatorial grid drawn of date)
nodes.rationale: Stars are placed once in J2000; precession and nutation appear because the Earth's axis moves inside the fixed sky. Exceptions: proper motion of fast stars and the of-date equatorial grid.

nodes.label: Geodetic observer pin on a unit sphere with ENU basis
nodes.rationale: The unit-sphere normal equals the WGS84 geodetic zenith Astronomy Engine uses, so altitudes match; cost is up to ~21 km in pin position.

nodes.label: Body directions: dirS (topocentric astrometric J2000) and geoDirS (geocentric)
Moon made astrometric (annual aberration removed from the geometric Moon)
nodes.rationale: The raw Moon sat ~20 arcsec off against the Sun and stars; corrected Sun-Moon separations are the apparent ones (9.2 arcsec at Luxor 2027-08-02, not 19).

nodes.label: Light-time correction
Topocentric directions (Moon parallax ~1 degree)
Astrometric J2000 drawing vs apparent of-date tables
nodes.rationale: The star catalogue is astrometric J2000 so beams land on the right stars; printed alt/az is what an observer measures. They differ by annual aberration (<=20.5 arcsec) and refraction.

nodes.label: True-scale Moon (IAU rotation, libration, Lommel-Seeliger lighting)
Solar system to scale with one linear scale (orrery)
nodes.rationale: A log scale was rejected: it bends Earth-to-planet lines away from true directions, so Mars would no longer be in Leo on the orrery while its beam says it is.

nodes.label: Orrery retrograde figure (24 sight lines, 2.5x backdrop)
Planet disc frame and impostor (discFrame/discView, oblate spheroid, Saturn's rings)
Jupiter's Galilean moons at light time (transit, occultation, eclipse, shadow flags)
Lunar libration and limb feature (AE.Libration)
Star sky catalogue (5,044 Hipparcos stars to mag 6, sky.json)
Telescope aperture gain (2*log10(25deg/FOV), up to 3.5 mag)
Star colour from B-V (Ballesteros + Planck x CIE 1931)
Guest stars: naked-eye supernovae of 1006-1604
Halley's Comet at five apparitions (two-body Kepler, illustrative tails)
B1950 -> J2000 element rotation (FK4 -> FK5, Standish 1982)
nodes.rationale: Without the rotation the 1986 node would be 0.7 degrees out.

nodes.label: Spacecraft ephemerides (Hermite knots, radio time, DSN view)
Near-Earth SGP4 satellites (TEME -> Earth-fixed via GMST, shadow, brightness, passes)
Linear proper motion of the 1,183 fast stars
nodes.rationale: Radial velocities are not in Hipparcos, so foreshortening is ignored; Arcturus in 1000 is within 1 arcmin of a rigorous space-motion calculation.

nodes.label: Pole and equinox of date (poleOfDate, equinoxOfDate)
Illustrative precession circle (25,772-year turn about the ecliptic pole)
Star cards: distance and when the light left (sigma-rounded)
Deep-sky objects (dso.json, illustrative visibility and sprites)
Max tier deeper stars (stars8.json, V 6-8)
Saemundsson refraction (refractionDeg)
Sky view refraction lift (refractLift, liftByRefraction, Bennett inverse for the Sun disc)
nodes.rationale: At SearchRiseSet's sunset the drawn upper limb now sits on the horizon instead of 0.84 degrees under the ground; eclipse geometry stays unrefracted.

nodes.label: Airmass and extinction (Kasten-Young, k = 0.2 mag)
Twilight classes by solar altitude
Sky-view exposure curves (stars, planets, Milky Way)
Star limit and starVisibility curve (star names share it)
Totality's star limit in magnitudes (about 2.0)
nodes.rationale: Specified in magnitudes so every tier shows the same stars; the old exposure term reached magnitude 5.7 on High and started 2.8 min before second contact.

nodes.label: Low Sun correction (Mie lobe tinted by extinction colour)
nodes.rationale: Preetham keeps a setting Sun's Mie glow nearly white, which washed the reddened disc out to cream on screen.

nodes.label: Illustrative landscape horizon (far ridge, trees or roofs, sea; seeded by place)
nodes.rationale: The far ridge is capped at 0.5 degrees since a 1.5-degree ridge would move sunset by minutes against the panel; the almanac and beams keep the mathematical horizon.

nodes.label: Night-sky brightness model (computeSkyglow, natural-sky units R = B/B_nat)
Walker's-law light pollution with city-core cap (16 azimuth bins)
Bortle class and Sky darkness setting
Limiting magnitude from SQM (Schaefer-type fit)
Zodiacal light and gegenschein (Leinert Table 17)
Night vision scotopic shift (adaptingLuminance, scotopicWeight)
Chromatic scintillation of low bright stars (twinkle)
Moonlight and moonglint on the globe's night side
nodes.rationale: Real moonlight is about 4e-6 of sunlight; the 0.02 gain is perceptual, like the clearer-than-life haze.

nodes.label: City lights at close zoom (cubic B-spline, hashed point field)
Sculpted clouds (height-field relief, Beer-powder, silver lining)
Aurora oval (IGRF centred dipole, Starkov boundaries, Kp setting)
nodes.rationale: Activity is a setting, not data: the app is offline-first with no external URLs, so it fetches no space-weather feed and says the oval is modelled, not a forecast.

nodes.label: World map: equirectangular, lit from the sphere (geocentric twilight contours)
Moon's parallax from two places (compareSight triangulation)
Rise, transit, set and twilight times
Tonight visibility verdicts and altitude series
Events search (quarters, oppositions, elongations, eclipses, seasons)
Retrograde paths and stationary points
Disc-overlap eclipse model (discVisible)
Sun angular radius at the live distance (not a constant 960 arcsec)
nodes.rationale: The constant 960 arcsec drew the 2027-08-02 umbra about 19% too narrow (104 km instead of 129 km half-width).

nodes.label: One eclipse geometry at the observer (contacts within 0.1 s of AE)
nodes.rationale: Obscuration, sky-view discs, flare and panel share the same two discs; before, drawn discs reached totality 35 s late at Luxor and the panel could read Partial 100.0%.

nodes.label: Eclipse-dimmed magnitudes (Sun obscuration, lunarEclipseLight quadrature)
Shadow-axis point P = m - t*s (shadowPoint)
Central solar eclipse path (eclipsePath on AE's ellipsoid, limits, citiesInPath)
Totality from the ground (Baily's beads, corona, chromosphere, 360-degree horizon)
nodes.rationale: Placed by the true contact geometry but shapes are illustrative: the lunar limb profile is not LOLA/Watts data and ignores libration.

nodes.label: Hand angles and 'Find it' directions (handSpan, findIt, ruler)
Pointing the phone (W3C DeviceOrientation, compass Align)
Moon-star occultations of five J2000 stars
Phase 6 events (Venus brilliancy, transits, lunar apsides, Saturn ring-plane crossings)
Meteor showers (IMO calendar, precession-corrected peaks, ZHR rates, drawn meteors)
Year planner (visibilityYear analytic altitudes)
Sun paths, analemma and subsolar figure-8 (sunFigures)
Standing on Mars: directions, IAU local frame, magnitudes
nodes.rationale: Sky colour and dust extinction are tuned by eye to rover images, not a radiative-transfer model; drawn low objects keep the Earth's refraction lift as a phase-1 simplification.
